propositions: Nested pytest child launched without --basetemp argument joins user-global numbered temp root, causing pytest session-finish cleanup to synchronously scan and delete stale temp trees, consuming the 90-second child timeout after test completes and [100%] is reported

Controlled A/B test with 400,000 stale shared-root entries shows private --basetemp child cleanup takes 0.882s versus shared-root child taking 10.800s, proving cleanup cost scales with retained entries

Real-subprocess regression oracle creates sentinel file in another run's temp tree; before fix nested pytest deletes sentinel (RED), after fix sentinel survives (GREEN), mutation back to omitted --basetemp returns to RED
Passing caller-owned tmp_path/nested-pytest via --basetemp to nested child isolates pytest cleanup without changing test selection, timeout, capture, or ambient-store assertions
